md_name: CoIP-MS Interaction Network Dataset in Cancer Cells
md_description: This workflow captures protein–protein interaction data from oncogenic mutant cancer cells using co-immunoprecipitation followed by mass spectrometry. It includes preparation of the cell material, antibody-based enrichment of protein complexes, spectral acquisition, and computational identification of interacting proteins under different experimental conditions. The resulting derived interaction tables support analysis of cancer-associated network rewiring and therapeutic target discovery.

cancer_cell_population.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the starting biological material: the cancer cell line/population identity, oncogenic mutation status, cancer type/context, and source/origin details. I excluded culture/treatment variables because those belong to the downstream experimental_conditioning Process, and I excluded enrichment, digestion, measurement, file, or computational fields because those belong to later Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there was nothing to avoid duplicating beyond staying within the entity territory. I also avoided sample/experiment identifiers unless they are needed to uniquely describe the cell population, since root-level identifiers are typically handled once in the dataset schema.

md_schema.descr: Name or label of the cancer cell population used as the starting material, e.g. HCT116, A549, MCF7. Record the exact cell line or primary tumor cell population identity at the time the workflow begins.

Cancer context for the starting cells, e.g. colorectal adenocarcinoma, lung adenocarcinoma, breast carcinoma. Use the biological disease category of the cell population rather than the treatment condition.

Whether the starting cancer cells carry an oncogenic mutation relevant to the experiment, recorded as the mutation state of the input population before conditioning; examples include mutant, wild_type_control, or mixed_population.
Gene symbol of the principal oncogenic driver altered in the starting population, e.g. KRAS, EGFR, TP53, BRAF. Record the specific gene that defines the mutation context of the input cells.
Specific mutation or alteration in the driver gene for the input cells, using standard protein or DNA notation where available, e.g. KRAS G12D, EGFR exon 19 deletion, TP53 R175H.
Biological origin of the starting cell material, indicating whether the cells are an established cell line, patient-derived cell line, or primary tumor-derived culture.
Species from which the cancer cells were derived, typically Homo sapiens for this workflow; record the organism identity of the starting material.
Source annotation for the starting material, such as tissue of origin or repository/provider if known. Record provenance of the cell population itself, not the experimental treatment applied later.

experimental_conditioning.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the cells were conditioned before capture: culture medium and key treatment parameters, stimulation/inhibition agent identity, dose, duration, and timing relative to capture. I also included process outcome/quality fields that help interpret whether conditioning succeeded, such as viability or response readouts, because those describe the process execution. I excluded intrinsic cell identity fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded antibody, capture, digestion, mass spectrometry, file, or computational fields because those belong to downstream Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided here, so there was no need to suppress duplicates.

md_schema.descr: Base culture medium used during the conditioning step, recorded as the exact formulation or standard medium name applied before capture, e.g. DMEM, RPMI 1640, with serum supplement if relevant.
Name of the treatment, stimulant, inhibitor, or other perturbation applied to modulate oncogenic signaling before protein complex capture, e.g. EGF, doxorubicin, MEK inhibitor.

Applied concentration of the conditioning agent at the moment of treatment, expressed in concentration units appropriate to the reagent, typically micromolar or nanogram per milliliter, and measured for the specific culture before capture.
Units for conditioning_agent_concentration, used to disambiguate the dose value; typical values include uM, nM, ng_per_ml, mM, and should match the reagent preparation used in this experiment.

Duration of exposure to the conditioning agent or culture condition before protein complex capture, measured from start of treatment to harvest; typical values range from minutes to many hours depending on signaling modulation.
Incubation temperature during the conditioning period, measured in degrees Celsius for the treated culture before capture, commonly 37 for mammalian cells.
CO2 percentage used during the conditioning incubation, measured as the atmospheric CO2 level in the culture environment before capture; typically around 5 percent for standard mammalian culture.
Whether the conditioning occurred immediately before capture or after a recovery period, recorded relative to the co-immunoprecipitation step to preserve the experimental timeline.

Optional process-level readout indicating whether the desired signaling perturbation was achieved during conditioning, such as pathway activation, inhibition, morphology change, or marker induction measured before capture.

Estimated percentage of viable cells at the end of conditioning, measured immediately before downstream capture to indicate whether treatment caused excessive toxicity; typical range is 0 to 100 percent.

conditioned_cancer_cells.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the conditioned biological material after the process step, so I included only properties of the resulting cell population itself: its condition state, harvest state, confluence, and whether it is freshly prepared or preserved for immediate use. I avoided repeating upstream source identity fields already associated with the starting cancer cell population, and I excluded protocol details such as treatment agent, dose, and duration because those belong to the experimental_conditioning Process. I also excluded capture, signal, and downstream analytical fields because this node is only the prepared biological input to co-immunoprecipitation. No already_generated fields were provided here beyond what was generated earlier, so I did not duplicate any of those terms semantically.

md_schema.descr: State of the cancer cells after the conditioning step and immediately before co-immunoprecipitation, indicating that the population is ready for capture; use this to distinguish treated, untreated, synchronized, or recovered cells.

Method used to collect the conditioned cells before immunoprecipitation input preparation, e.g. adherent scraping, trypsinization, centrifugation, or direct lysis; record the physical harvest approach applied to the cell population.
Approximate cell confluence at the time of harvest, reported as a percentage of the culture surface covered by cells immediately before capture input preparation; typical range is 0 to 100 percent.
Time elapsed from the end of experimental conditioning to the harvest of the cells for co-immunoprecipitation input, measured in hours and recorded when relevant to preserve the state of signaling.
Boolean flag indicating whether this conditioned cell population was successfully prepared and routed to the co-immunoprecipitation capture step.
Current handling state of the conditioned cells after harvest and before capture, such as fresh, frozen, or thawed, recorded to capture whether the material was used immediately or stored briefly.

coimmunoprecipitation_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the instrument/assay session configuration and actively controlled parameters for the co-immunoprecipitation step: bait antibody identity, bead/solid support, binding and wash conditions, elution approach, and platform-specific settings. I also included hardware/agent descriptors for the capture setup as required by the rules, such as instrument or platform name, manufacturer, model, and serial number when applicable. I excluded cell-line origin, treatment history, and the resulting enriched material's file-like or physical properties, because those belong upstream to the Entity node or downstream to the Signal node. I also avoided duplicating any fields from earlier nodes, especially treatment parameters and conditioned-cell state, and I kept output-only properties like recovered sample file paths or spectral data out of this Capture node.

md_schema.descr: Name of the immunoprecipitation platform or workstation used to perform the capture, recorded as the configured hardware or bench setup responsible for the co-immunoprecipitation session.
Manufacturer of the co-immunoprecipitation platform or associated automation hardware, recorded to identify the configured instrument environment used during capture.
Model name or number of the platform used for antibody-based enrichment, e.g. magnetic rack system, automated immunoprecipitation robot, or liquid handling module.
Serial number of the capture platform or major hardware component used for the immunoprecipitation session, recorded exactly as on the instrument label when available.
Name of the antibody used as the bait for immunoprecipitation, recorded at the capture step as the configured reagent that determines the protein complex target, e.g. anti-TP53, anti-HA, anti-Myc.
Host species in which the bait antibody was raised, recorded for capture specificity and downstream interpretation, e.g. mouse, rabbit, goat.
Antibody isotype used for the capture reagent, recorded as part of the immunoprecipitation configuration, e.g. IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b, IgG.
Amount of bait antibody used per capture reaction, reported in micrograms at the time the immunoprecipitation is assembled; typical values depend on target abundance and bead capacity.
Solid support used to immobilize the antibody during co-immunoprecipitation, recorded as the bead chemistry or carrier type, e.g. protein A agarose, protein G magnetic beads.
Volume of bead slurry or bead suspension used per capture reaction, measured in microliters at assembly time; typical range depends on bead capacity and sample input.
Composition of the lysis or binding buffer used during co-immunoprecipitation capture, including key detergents, salts, and pH if controlled for the assay.
Temperature at which the conditioned cell lysate and bait antibody were incubated during capture, measured in degrees Celsius for the immunoprecipitation session.
Duration of the antibody-antigen binding incubation during co-immunoprecipitation, measured from reaction assembly to bead separation in minutes.
Composition of the wash buffer used to remove non-specific binders after immunoprecipitation, recorded as the configured buffer formulation used for the capture session.
Number of wash cycles applied to the beads during the co-immunoprecipitation capture step, counted as the total washes before elution.
Method used to release the enriched protein complexes from the immunoprecipitation beads, e.g. low pH elution, SDS sample buffer, competitive peptide, or heat elution.

Capture-level quality indication for the immunoprecipitation session, recorded as a brief assessment such as successful enrichment, weak pull-down, or high background based on the operator's or platform's readout.

enriched_protein_complex_signal.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw material/file-like properties of the enriched protein-complex sample recovered from capture and prepared for MS input: sample format, storage location, aliquot information, volume/mass, and technical quality metrics describing the physical artefact itself. I excluded bait antibody, bead, wash, and incubation details because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded digestion and mass spectrometry settings because those belong to downstream Process and Capture nodes. I also avoided biological interpretation or protein-identification fields, since this node is only the recovered raw input material. No already_generated fields were provided here that overlap semantically with these signal descriptors.

md_schema.descr: Physical presentation of the recovered enriched protein-complex material as prepared for mass spectrometry input, e.g. eluate, dried pellet, or buffer-resuspended sample, recorded immediately after co-immunoprecipitation recovery.
Volume of the enriched protein-complex sample aliquot submitted or stored for downstream digestion or MS preparation, measured in microliters for the recovered signal material.

Estimated protein mass in the recovered enriched complex sample, measured in micrograms at the time the sample is prepared for mass spectrometry input; use this to describe the quantity of captured material.
Physical or inventory location where the recovered enriched protein-complex sample is stored before digestion or mass spectrometry, e.g. freezer shelf, rack, box position, or laboratory sample ID.
Storage temperature of the recovered enriched protein-complex sample before downstream processing, measured in degrees Celsius; typical values include -80, -20, or 4 depending on handling.

Technical format of the digital record associated with this raw sample signal when applicable, e.g. vendor export, spreadsheet, or text record describing the recovered material. Use only if the signal is represented by a managed file artifact.
Quality flag for the recovered enriched protein-complex material, recorded as a raw-signal status such as clean recovery, low yield, contamination suspected, or degraded sample before digestion.

Optional numeric integrity assessment of the recovered material at the time it is prepared for downstream processing, using the laboratory's internal scale if available; record only if a standardized score is assigned to this signal artifact.

proteolytic_digest.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the enriched protein material was converted into peptides: protease identity, digestion conditions, enzyme-to-substrate ratio, buffer/additive choices, reduction/alkylation settings, and a process-quality indicator. I excluded the input sample’s quantity and storage properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded peptide file properties and mass spectrometry settings because those belong downstream to the peptide Entity and MS Capture nodes. I also excluded any protein-identification outputs, since this process only performs digestion and does not yet interpret the results. No already_generated fields were provided for this node, so I did not need to suppress overlaps beyond keeping the scope strictly procedural.

md_schema.descr: Name of the proteolytic enzyme used to digest the enriched protein material into peptides, e.g. trypsin, Lys-C, Glu-C; record the enzyme identity applied at the digestion step.
Amount ratio of protease to enriched protein substrate used during digestion, recorded at the time of reaction setup, commonly expressed as 1:50, 1:100, or similar laboratory ratio.
Composition of the buffer used for proteolytic digestion, including pH and major reagents if controlled, recorded as the reaction medium that supports peptide generation.
Whether a reducing agent was applied before or during digestion to break disulfide bonds, recorded as a process setting for peptide preparation.
Whether an alkylation step was applied after reduction to block free thiols, recorded as a process setting for peptide preparation.
Temperature at which the proteolytic digestion was carried out, measured in degrees Celsius during the peptide-generation reaction, typically 37 for tryptic digestion.
Total time allowed for proteolytic digestion, measured in hours from enzyme addition to reaction quench or completion.
Orbital shaking or agitation speed used during digestion, measured in revolutions per minute if the protocol uses active mixing.
Expected or tolerated number of missed cleavage sites in the digestion process, recorded as a digestion-design parameter relevant to peptide completeness.
Process-level quality assessment of the digestion reaction, such as complete digestion, partial digestion, or overdigestion, recorded after the reaction is finished.

peptide_mixture.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the digest-derived peptide material, so I included intrinsic sample properties of the peptide mixture itself: preparation state, peptide concentration or amount, desalting status, complexity/length characteristics, and whether the material is ready for instrument injection. I excluded digestion protocol settings because those belong to the upstream proteolytic_digest Process, and I excluded LC-MS acquisition settings because those belong to the downstream Capture node. I also avoided raw file properties and computational identification fields, since this node is a physical sample entity rather than a signal or derivative. No already_generated fields were provided for this node, so there was no duplication to resolve beyond keeping the scope centered on the peptide material.

md_schema.descr: Preparation state of the digest-derived peptide material submitted for MS analysis, indicating whether it is dissolved, dried, desalted, or otherwise ready for injection.
Concentration of peptides in the mixture prepared for instrument analysis, measured in nanograms per microliter at the time the sample is loaded or queued for MS.
Total amount of peptide material available in the mixture, measured in micrograms for the sample submitted to the instrument.
Whether the peptide mixture underwent desalting or cleanup before mass spectrometry, recorded as the preparation state of the peptide entity.

Approximate peptide length range represented in the mixture, measured in amino acid residues for the digest-derived sample; typical tryptic peptides often fall within a moderate length range suitable for MS.
Boolean flag indicating whether the peptide mixture passed preparation checks and was ready for mass spectrometry capture or injection.
Brief note describing the observed complexity of the peptide mixture, such as low complexity, moderate complexity, or highly complex, used as an intrinsic description of the sample entity.

mass_spectrometry_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for mass spectrometry: instrument identity, manufacturer/model/serial number, ionization and analyzer settings, LC and acquisition parameters, and calibrated detection settings. I also included capture-level performance indicators such as mass accuracy or resolution because they describe the configured measurement quality, not the resulting data file. I excluded peptide sample properties from the upstream Entity node, and I excluded raw file format, storage, and dimensionality because those belong to the downstream raw_ms_spectra Signal node. I also avoided computational identification parameters, since those belong later to spectral_processing. No already_generated fields were provided for this node, so there was no duplication to avoid beyond keeping to the capture territory.

md_schema.descr: Name of the mass spectrometer used to acquire the raw spectra from the peptide mixture, recorded as the configured instrument for this capture session, e.g. Orbitrap Exploris 480, Q Exactive HF, timsTOF Pro.
Manufacturer of the mass spectrometer, recorded for the capture instrumentation used in this session, e.g. Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bruker, Sciex.
Model number or model name of the mass spectrometer used for data acquisition, recorded at the time of capture to identify the instrument configuration.
Serial number of the mass spectrometer used in this capture session, recorded exactly as assigned by the manufacturer when available.
Ionization mode used to generate ions from the peptide mixture during MS capture, typically electrospray in positive mode for proteomics workflows.
Type of mass analyzer used during acquisition, recorded as the configured analyzer for the capture session, e.g. Orbitrap, TOF, ion trap, FT-ICR.
Liquid chromatography mode used inline with MS capture, recorded as the separation setup applied to the peptide mixture before or during ionization, e.g. nanoLC.
Acquisition strategy used during the mass spectrometry session, recorded as the configured method for measuring the peptide mixture, e.g. data-dependent or data-independent acquisition.
Mass-to-charge range scanned during acquisition, measured in m/z units for the configured mass spectrometry session; record the range used to capture peptide ions.
Fragmentation technique used during tandem MS acquisition, recorded as the configured method for generating peptide fragment ions, e.g. HCD, CID, ETD.
Resolution setting used during MS acquisition, recorded as the configured instrument resolution for the capture session; use the instrument's native units or setting description.
Collision energy applied during fragmentation, measured in electronvolts or instrument-native equivalent settings for the MS capture session.
Total duration of the mass spectrometry acquisition run, measured in minutes from injection or start of acquisition to completion.
Instrument-level mass accuracy achieved during the capture session, measured in parts per million as a technical performance indicator of the configured MS run.
Configured signal-to-noise threshold used for detection or inclusion during acquisition, recorded as part of the capture session settings.

raw_ms_spectra.reasoning: I fixed the cross-step collision by removing technical_quality_flag from this Signal node, since that field name was already generated earlier in the DAG. I kept the rest of the schema within the raw spectral signal territory: file format, size, scan count, dimensionality, retention-time and m/z coverage, storage location, checksum, and a raw-signal intensity metric. I did not add any process, capture, or derivative fields, and I avoided reusing any semantically equivalent quality flag name that would duplicate the earlier field.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw mass spectral artefact produced by the instrument, recorded as the vendor or export format used to store the spectrum data, e.g. RAW, mzML, mzXML.
Size of the raw spectral data file, measured in bytes at the time it is stored or transferred; use this to describe the technical scale of the artefact.
Dimensionality of the raw spectral data representation, describing whether the artefact contains one-dimensional MS1 scans, tandem MS2 scans, or combined multi-stage data.
Total number of spectra or scans contained in the raw mass spectrometry file, counted for the artefact produced by this capture session.
Range of chromatographic retention times covered by the raw spectral acquisition, measured in minutes for the full raw data file.
Observed mass-to-charge range represented in the raw spectra, recorded as the technical m/z span of the artefact rather than the instrument setting.
Digital storage location of the raw spectral file, such as a local path, network path, or repository URI where the artefact is archived.
Checksum of the raw spectral file used to verify artefact integrity during transfer or archiving, recorded as an MD5 hash string if available.
Highest observed peak intensity in the raw spectra, recorded as a technical signal metric for the raw artefact and not as a biological result.

spectral_processing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational workflow that transforms raw spectra into peptide/protein assignments: software identity, version, repository, search/database parameters, scoring thresholds, FDR control, and output-level process quality indicators. I excluded raw file properties and instrument acquisition settings because those belong to the upstream Signal and Capture nodes, respectively. I also avoided any final interaction-network interpretation because that belongs to the downstream Derivative nodes. The earlier collision note means I should not reuse technical_quality_flag; instead I used process-specific QC names that describe the software step without duplicating prior fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the analysis software used to process the raw spectra, recorded at the spectral-processing step, e.g. MaxQuant, Proteome Discoverer, MSFragger, Mascot.
Version of the analysis software used for spectral processing, recorded exactly as run for peptide and protein identification.
Repository or source reference for the analysis software used in processing, e.g. vendor site, GitHub URL, or package source; record where the exact version came from.
Protein sequence database used for spectral searching, recorded as the exact reference database applied to infer peptide and protein IDs, e.g. UniProt human proteome, custom FASTA.
Version date or release date of the search database used during spectral processing, recorded to allow reproduction of peptide/protein identification results.
Proteolytic specificity assumed by the search engine during peptide identification, recorded as the in silico cleavage rule used for database searching.
List of fixed chemical modifications applied in the database search, recorded as the peptide search setting used during spectral processing, e.g. carbamidomethylation.
List of variable modifications allowed in the database search, recorded as the peptide search setting used during spectral processing, e.g. oxidation, phosphorylation.
Allowed precursor mass tolerance used for spectral matching, measured in parts per million at the search stage.
Allowed fragment ion mass tolerance used for spectral matching, measured in daltons at the search stage.
Minimum peptide-spectrum match score or equivalent cutoff required for accepting identifications, recorded as the processing threshold used in this workflow.
Maximum false discovery rate allowed for protein-level inference from spectral matches, recorded as a proportion or percentage threshold used during processing.
Decoy database or target-decoy strategy used to estimate false discoveries during spectral processing, recorded as the identification validation approach.
Process-level confidence category assigned to the spectral identification workflow, such as high confidence or exploratory, based on the search and filtering results.

protein_identification_results.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed results from the spectral processing step: identified proteins, peptide assignments, scores/confidence, coverage, abundance-like quantities, and condition-specific result summaries. I excluded software, database, and search settings because those belong to the upstream spectral_processing Process. I also excluded raw file and instrument properties because those belong to earlier Signal and Capture nodes, and I did not include final network assembly or biological interpretation because that belongs to the downstream interaction_network_assembly Process and interaction_network_table Derivative. I avoided reusing the earlier collision field technical_quality_flag and used result-specific quality metrics instead.

md_schema.descr: Primary accession or identifier of a protein inferred from the mass spectra, recorded as the computed result for a given experimental condition, e.g. UniProt accession.
Common name or gene-based label of the inferred protein, reported as part of the derivative identification result for each condition.
Peptide sequence assigned to the identified protein from the spectral search, recorded as the computed amino acid sequence inferred from the raw spectra.
Score or confidence value for the peptide-spectrum match that supports the identification, recorded as the derivative confidence metric for the inferred peptide assignment.
Sequence coverage of the identified protein by matched peptides, measured as the percentage of the protein sequence explained by the spectral evidence.
Number of proteins identified for a given experimental condition after spectral processing and filtering, recorded as a summary count of the derivative output.
Experimental condition associated with the protein identification result, e.g. untreated, mutant_A, inhibitor_treated, used to partition the derivative output by comparison group.
Computed abundance-like score or intensity-based metric assigned to the identified protein by the processing pipeline, recorded as a derivative quantitative estimate.
Estimated false discovery rate for the identified protein result set, expressed as a percentage or equivalent proportion derived from the search and filtering pipeline.
Categorical status of the protein identification result, indicating whether the inferred protein passed filtering and was accepted for downstream analysis.

interaction_network_assembly.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational assembly of interaction networks from already identified proteins: software used for network construction, merge/integration strategy across conditions, scoring and edge-selection parameters, and summary QC of the assembled network. I excluded raw spectra, peptide assignments, and protein-identification details because those belong to upstream Signal and Derivative nodes. I also excluded the final interaction table's explicit row-level annotations, because those belong to the downstream interaction_network_table Derivative. I avoided duplicating process software fields already used in spectral_processing by using network-specific parameter names rather than repeating generic software metadata where unnecessary.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to assemble interaction networks from the identified protein lists, recorded at the network-construction step, e.g. Cytoscape, igraph pipeline, custom R script.
Version of the network assembly software or pipeline used to integrate identified proteins across conditions, recorded exactly as executed for this process step.
Repository, package source, or code location for the network assembly method used to build the interaction network, recorded to support reproducibility of the derived network construction.
Method used to consolidate identified proteins across experimental conditions into a unified interaction network, e.g. union, intersection, condition-specific layering, or weighted merging.
Approach used to score or rank candidate protein-protein interaction edges during network assembly, recorded as the algorithmic rule applied to the identified protein evidence.
Threshold used to include or exclude an interaction edge in the assembled network, recorded as the cutoff applied during network construction.
Definition of the condition comparison used to identify mutation-dependent network changes, recorded as the control-versus-perturbation design applied during assembly.
Total number of nodes in the assembled interaction network, counted after consolidation across conditions and before export to the table derivative.
Total number of edges in the assembled interaction network, counted after the interaction assembly process has applied its inclusion criteria.
Process-level quality assessment for the assembled interaction network, such as sparse, well-connected, noisy, or high-confidence, recorded after assembly and before table export.

interaction_network_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I kept only table-level computed outputs that summarize the assembled interaction network. Because condition_label already existed in a previous DAG step, I removed it and replaced it with a non-colliding table-specific condition reference, while retaining interaction partner identity, bait/antibody context as annotations, detection method annotation, network role, confidence, support count, and interpretive labels. I excluded upstream raw/capture/process fields and avoided repeating root-level identifiers. I also kept the schema focused on the exported network table rather than the software or assembly settings that produced it.

md_schema.descr: Name or label of the protein recorded as an interaction partner in the derived network table, summarized from the assembled interaction network for downstream interpretation.
Protein accession or database identifier for the interaction partner listed in the table, e.g. UniProt accession, recorded as the derived identifier for the network row.
Name of the bait protein or target used to generate the interaction network entry, recorded in the final derived table as the biological query associated with the interaction partner.

Reference to the experimental condition associated with the interaction record, such as a study-specific condition code or label, used to stratify entries in the derived network table without reusing a prior DAG field name.
Antibody name listed in the final network table as an annotation for the interaction record, summarizing the bait antibody used during capture.
Detection method annotation carried into the final table, e.g. mass spectrometry, western blot validation, or other downstream detection label associated with the interaction row.
Role assigned to the protein within the interaction network table, such as bait, prey, hub, or connector, based on the assembled network structure and biological interpretation.
Computed confidence score or weight for the interaction represented in the table, derived from the assembly process and used to rank network associations.
Number of experimental observations or evidential peptides supporting the interaction entry in the derived table, recorded as a count summarizing support for the network edge.

Short interpretive annotation attached to the interaction entry, such as mutation-dependent gain, mutation-dependent loss, or candidate therapeutic target, used for downstream biological interpretation.
Unique row identifier for the interaction table entry, used to track each derived interaction record within the exported network table; format example: row_001 or network_000123.
